gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus's '6,000 W' is available only through its 120/240 V L14-30R twist-lock outlet: its standard 120 V outlets are rated '120V~ 20A Max … 2400W Max', and 240 V output 'cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC'. The makers also rate cycle life to different end points: BLUETTI says 6,000 cycles to 80% retention, while Anker gives '3,000+ cycles' with no end point.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts 'Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts' (cited, 2026-11-08), StormWatts '5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input' (rank 1–8, 2026-11-16) and Anker's own F3800 Plus kit page (cited). The same-panel-watts article lists no AC output, surge or cycle life for any of its 24 kits. The solar-input article says it found no per-outlet limits for any unit and no continuous/surge split for the Jackery or the F3800 Plus. It gives the Anker S5000's 10,000 cycles without the capacity it is rated to, and says the other cycle ratings are 'Not stated'. Neither article puts cycle ratings on the same end point or separates 120 V outlet watts from the 240 V nameplate total. I could not load three other pages: theoutageready.com and solargenadvisor.com (certificate error) and solargenreview.com (HTTP 429). So I cannot rule out that one of them has this point.
decides: This undercuts ChatGPT's main reason for its first pick ('lean toward the Anker F3800 Plus because of its 6,000W output'). A shopper plugging 120 V appliances into the unit gets at most 2,400 W from any one outlet. The 6 kW figure needs the L14-30R outlet feeding a transfer switch or inlet box, and that outlet goes dead while the unit charges from a 120 V wall outlet. By contrast, BLUETTI rates the Apex 300 at 3,840 W continuous and says it powers 120 V and 240 V devices at the same time, with cycle life rated to 80% rather than to an unstated end point. On the same 80% basis, the Apex 300's battery outlasts any rating Anker publishes. The pick should rest on watts at the outlet the shopper will actually use, cycle life on a stated end point, and whether the kit ships now. The F3800 Plus is sold out, and Anker's 400 W panels ship in early December. The Jackery 5000 Plus is on pre-order to ship Dec 2, with the 500X panels by Dec 5. The Apex 300 ships in late January. That favours a large kit that ships now, such as the BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit (5,120 Wh, 5,000 W, link price $3,799.05, ships now per the kits table) or the ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP039 (link price $1,753.93, ships now), over the 240 V pre-orders.
